population.note: FICTIONAL. ~262M US adults; 9.2% current = ~24.1M users. Arithmetic: of 16.0% ever-users, 4.8 pts never stopped and are on now; 11.2 pts (70%, consistent with ~1/3 one-year persistence) stopped at least once; 5.0 pts of those (45%, inside the 36–47% restart range) restarted, 4.4 pts are on now and 0.6 pts stopped again; current = 4.8 + 4.4 = 9.2; off now = 11.2 − 4.4 = 6.8 = 16.0 − 9.2; cycled = 5.0/16.0 = 31%. Point prevalence is also pulled down by drug holidays: in survey data about one in eight users reports being on a planned break in the week asked, and many say they are 'off' even though they will be back on next month. Age-weighted check (adult shares 20/33/24/23%): 0.70+2.48+3.84+2.19 ≈ 9.2. The decline is concentrated in 50–64-year-olds with commercial insurance (22%→16%) after employers dropped coverage. The 65+ figure holds steady because Medicare kept paying. Payer mix of the 24.1M current users: commercial/employer ~8.0M (mostly diabetes and cardiac codes), Medicare all indications ~5.5M, Medicaid ~3.0M, brand cash (TrumpRx/direct) ~5.5M, non-FDA-approved product (imports, counterfeits, remaining compounders) ~2.1M; total 24.1M. Bottom income third sits lowest despite the Medicaid subsidy, because fewer than half of states took it up and gray-market users under-report. Children: ~0.3% of under-18s, still skewed to upper-income households. The 6.8% of adults who used and are now off are about 17.8M people, the largest group of former users in the drug's history.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot ended on schedule in Dec 2027. It was replaced from Jan 2028 by a CMS Part D demonstration at the same $245/month negotiated price, of which the beneficiary pays $50 and Medicare $195, under the same BMI and comorbidity criteria. ~1.7M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 1.7M × $195 × 12 ≈ $4.0B/yr federal. Medicaid: under the GLP-1 Access Match (Nov 2027) the federal government pays 100% of the $245 drug cost for states that opt in, with a $0 copay, for obesity with comorbidity or for alcohol use disorder. 24 states opted in, ~1.3M enrollees: 1.3M × $245 × 12 ≈ $3.8B/yr federal. Together that is ~$7.8B/yr, above the pace of CBO's original ≥$35B/2026–34 score, and CBO rescored the program in 2028.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India $8–48/month, 60+ brands; Canada generic semaglutide CAD 80–110/month from four makers; Brazil and Mexico generics widely sold; generic injectable semaglutide in ~160 countries. These are the source of the US import stream.
access.note: Brand cash prices stepped down through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels: oral starter doses $149, maintenance orals and injectables $199–299. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349 and almost nobody pays it. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 60% to 44% (Business Group on Health, 2028). Covering plans increasingly require a diabetes, cardiovascular, sleep-apnea or MASH code, so coverage for obesity alone is the main thing lost. The result is two tiers: coded patients pay a copay, everyone else pays $149–299 a month in cash or turns to imports. The gray market went from 'contained' to 'significant' as Canadian and Indian generics arrived by mail, through cross-border trips and through counterfeit pens sold on social commerce. About 2.1M people (~9% of users) are on non-FDA-approved product.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1/amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Dec 2026)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved May 2028)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder with comorbid obesity — guideline-endorsed (ASAM/VA-DoD, Jun 2027), not an FDA label; Novo AUD phase 3 under way
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol use disorder without obesity, prescribed on the strength of the 2027 guidelines
planned 'drug holidays' and weekend skipping to restore enjoyment or save money
low-dose 'maintenance' use by people without obesity via telehealth
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
nicotine and gambling craving reduction, observational
drugs.pipeline_note: CagriSema was approved Dec 2026 (~20%) but has taken little share from tirzepatide. Retatrutide's BLA was filed Mar 2027 and approved May 2028, 14 months later, at ~28% mean loss, with a dysesthesia warning from its trials and a slow, tightly prior-authorised launch at $299 cash. The muscle-preserving driver is honoured under the approval rules by a filing, not a US launch. Lilly's bimagrumab + tirzepatide phase 3 read out in Apr 2028 (roughly 90% of weight lost as fat vs ~70% on tirzepatide alone) and was filed under priority review in Aug 2028, with a decision expected 2029. Marketing, fitness chains and clinicians already speak of the 'skinny-frail' problem as solved before any approval. Amycretin is still in phase 3, with no filing. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 and not on the market. The global incretin market is growing more slowly than 2026 forecasts because US volume is flat and ex-US prices are generic.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Re-escalation after drug holidays brings repeated bouts of GI symptoms, and users cite this as a cost of cycling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; re-titration guidance added to prescribing information after missed doses.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; retatrutide trials consistent.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
~25–30% of lost weight is lean mass on current approved drugs. The bimagrumab combination data have not been approved or reviewed by FDA, but they have changed public perception faster than practice.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on approved products; combination under priority review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; no new data resolved it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a mainstream complaint. Survey self-report puts it at roughly 1 in 5 long-term users describing muted enjoyment at some point, but there is still no prospective trial measuring it. The AUD guideline rests on the same mechanism.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on labels; ASAM guideline notes 'monitor mood and motivation'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world and trial figures still conflict. Holiday-takers report partial regain of appetite within 7–10 days of stopping.
More case reports, no definitive study.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects >5 years; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of RCT follow-up now exists. Nearly a third of ever-users have cycled, but there are still no controlled data on cycling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; NIH cycling cohort funded 2028.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Product harm, not a new drug signal. The Sep 2027 CDC cluster involved insulin-filled counterfeit pens and bacterially contaminated vials: 340+ ED visits in 14 states and 4 deaths. More than 5,000 FDA adverse-event reports now tie to non-approved product. Dosing errors with Indian multi-dose vials are common.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Advisory; FDA import alert on unapproved semaglutide; CBP mail seizures; state AG actions against social-commerce sellers; personal-importation enforcement remains discretionary.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume losses in snacks and sugary drinks continue but have flattened, because US current-user share fell slightly while ever-user households keep their habits. Portion-reduced and high-protein formats are now standard, not niche. 'GLP-1-friendly' as a label is fading because it has become the default.

alcohol.state: The 2027 AUD guideline gives heavy drinkers a medical pathway that reaches exactly the top-decile customers. Spirits volumes keep falling, with on-premise holding up better than off-premise. Brown-Forman and Diageo have cut US guidance again and are pushing no- and low-alcohol lines and premium 'occasion' pricing.

restaurants.state: Traffic holds; check sizes flat. Small-plate and half-portion menus are universal in casual dining. Cocktail sales are down and dessert sharing is up.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, though more slowly. Cyclers drive a 'two-size closet' trade and resale platforms report the strongest volumes in size-shifted inventory.

fitness.state: Strength-training chains market 'muscle insurance' and pre-sell the coming combination drug. Gyms sell holiday-month 'reset' packages to users on breaks.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is at 44%. Plans that still cover require diabetes or cardiac codes plus step therapy through orals. Public payers now carry the obesity-only patients, but only where they qualify.

pharma.state: The Lilly–Novo duopoly holds the US with retatrutide and CagriSema added. US net prices are down about 40% since 2025, volume is flat, and ex-US revenue is lost to generics. Revenue is still growing on new launches, but more slowly than 2026 forecasts.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured professionals over 40, being on it is unremarkable and being visibly off it draws the questions: 'Lost your coverage? On a holiday?' A body regaining weight reads as a lapse in coverage more than in will.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Two tiers are visible. Coded patients and the cash-comfortable are on brand drugs. Uncoded working-class users pay $149 for starter doses they never escalate from, or buy imports. In Phoenix and Tucson, Nogales pharmacy trips for 'Mexican Ozempic' have become ordinary errands.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared plates and smaller portions are the norm. Holiday weekends, when people take breaks, have become feast occasions again, and families plan Thanksgiving around who is 'off that week'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps in big metros added an optional 'on / off / cycling' field in 2028. Couples talk openly about timing holidays around anniversaries and trips to get desire back.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a dial you can adjust; the 2027 AUD guidelines extended that frame to drinking. Wanting things is discussed as a dose question.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Self-reported by roughly one in five long-term users at some point (survey, not trial). Dose reduction and scheduled holidays are the standard response; clinicians routinely ask 'how's your enjoyment?' at follow-up.
interior_life.framing: A side effect to be managed. Addiction medicine, under the AUD guideline, calls the same effect treatment. Users describe it as something they can turn up or down.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some sales and creative-agency staff take weekends off the drug and describe Mondays as 'flat for a day'. Some users credit quieter craving with steadier focus. There is no employer policy either way.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians joke about performing 'between doses'. Sour, spicy and extreme-flavour foods remain a growth niche. Bar trivia nights report sober regulars who used to be heavy drinkers.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is the most common reason given for holidays among under-50s. Couples schedule breaks around trips.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Price, not personality, is the political issue: the Canada and Nogales import trips and the Sep 2027 counterfeit deaths. A small libertarian-left campaign argues that 'pharmacological temperance' is being pushed through Medicaid AUD prescribing, but it is marginal.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access for approved brands, hostile to unapproved product. FDA import alerts and CBP mail seizures, but personal importation is prosecuted only for resale.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Subsidy, no mandate. The Medicaid GLP-1 Access Match pays 100% of the $245 drug cost at a $0 copay in 24 opt-in states, for obesity with comorbidity or AUD. The Medicare Part D demonstration continues the Bridge terms at $245/$50.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage is conditioned on BMI or comorbidity codes and prior authorisation. Some Medicaid states require a 6-month weight or AUD-outcome check to renew. There is no adherence surveillance.
state.workforce_or_military: Army and Navy accession guidance (2027) admits recruits who met body-composition standards on a GLP-1 if they have been off it for 90 days and are stable. Otherwise none.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US–Canada price gap (about $199–299 brand vs CAD 80–110 generic) is a cross-border political issue. Ottawa has limited bulk export of generic semaglutide under its drug-shortage rules. India is the source of most mail-order and counterfeit-adjacent supply.

prose.headline: Off Is the New On: Fewer Americans take GLP-1s, more have tried them, and everyone wants to know why you stopped
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 a smaller share of American adults is on an incretin drug than two years earlier, about 9 in 100 rather than 11. More people have tried one, though, and the country is more comfortable with the drugs than ever. The fall is not a backlash. It comes mostly from benefits managers, plus a habit. Employers kept dropping weight-loss coverage, from 60 percent to 44 percent of large firms. The plans that still pay mostly want a diabetes, heart, sleep-apnea or liver code on the claim. A 54-year-old with obesity and nothing else coded on her chart now pays cash, and cash has come down only part way. The government deals keep brand drugs between $149 and $299 a month. That is affordable at the starter dose and a strain at the dose that works.

The habit is the holiday. Muted enjoyment, the 'Ozempic personality', went from a curiosity in a few newspapers to something people ask about at dinner. The standard response is now cultural rather than clinical: lower the dose, skip the weekend, take a month off for the wedding. At any given moment about one in eight users is on a planned break. Nearly a third of everyone who has ever used the drugs has stopped and started again. Among insured professionals over forty, being on one is as unremarkable as statins. Visible regain gets a sympathetic question about coverage, not a judgment about willpower.

Washington spends more than it planned. The Medicare pilot ended on schedule in December 2027 and its terms simply continued under a new demonstration: $245 a month, $50 from the patient. In November 2027 HHS offered states full federal payment for Medicaid enrollees with obesity and a comorbidity, or with alcohol use disorder. Twenty-four states accepted. Together about three million people get the drug through those two doors, at a federal cost near $8 billion a year, and CBO has had to rescore.

Alcohol is the new frontier. In June 2027 the addiction-medicine guidelines endorsed semaglutide for heavy drinkers with obesity. That is not yet an FDA label, but it is enough for Medicaid and the VA to prescribe. Spirits companies have cut their forecasts again. Their best customers now have a medical reason to drink less, and some bars notice regulars who order soda and stay for trivia.

The price gap with Canada and India is now a supply line. Generic semaglutide costs about eighty Canadian dollars across the northern border and a few dollars in Indian pharmacies, and it arrives by mail and by day trip. Some two million Americans use unapproved product. In September 2027 the CDC traced insulin-filled counterfeit pens and contaminated vials to hundreds of emergency visits and four deaths. The FDA issued an import alert and customs seizes parcels, but demand has not moved, because the cash price has not.

The industry has a new story. Lilly's retatrutide, approved in May, takes off more than a quarter of body weight. Its experimental pairing of tirzepatide with the muscle-building antibody bimagrumab is under FDA review. Gyms, ads and doctors already talk as if 'skinny-frail' is a solved problem, although no approved product has solved it. Food companies have stopped printing 'GLP-1 friendly' on packages because smaller portions are now simply how food is sold.

Nothing has collapsed. Snacks sell less, plus-size stores keep closing, and restaurants serve half-plates at full prices. Children with obesity in affluent suburbs are a little more likely to be prescribed than they were. The open questions are the ones from 2026: what a decade of switching appetite on and off does to a body, and who decides when wanting less counts as treatment.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Ortega takes her pill at 6:10 before her coffee, as the Foundayo box tells her to. It is the lowest dose, $149 a month on her card, ever since the dental group's new plan dropped her Zepbound in January. The hygienists call it 'the coupon dose.' It mostly works.

It's Friday, so she leaves the Saturday pill in the foil. She has done this since spring. Raúl says she laughs at the TV again on Sundays.

At the front desk she confirms a patient's Medicaid. The woman says she gets 'the shot' free now, for drinking, and that she sleeps. Marisol nods and tells her about the bleeding-gum pamphlet.

At lunch her sister texts a photo of her husband Beto, upright on the couch. He's home. The pens from the Nogales guy were insulin, and he spent two days in the hospital at Banner. Her sister writes: Never again. Marisol writes: Canada mail is safer. She deletes it and sends a heart instead.

Her mother calls from Medicare's $50 line about whether the pharmacy closes at six. It does.

At Costco she buys the half-size enchilada tray and a whole tres leches, because Saturday.

At dinner her son, sixteen and round-faced like Raúl was, asks if he'll have to take it. She says ask the doctor. He says the doctor's a pill. Raúl laughs.

At eleven she is hungry, properly hungry. She stands at the open fridge longer than she needs to, just to feel it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: US net prices are down about 40% since 2025, volume is flat, and ex-US revenue is lost to generics.
least_plausible_claims.why: Net price down 40% with flat volume cannot produce growing revenue, and the candidate's own user count fell from about 28.8M (11%) to 24.1M. The 'still growing on new launches' claim is asserted with no arithmetic, so this fails mechanism and reconciliation.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Lilly's bimagrumab + tirzepatide phase 3 read out in Apr 2028 (roughly 90% of weight lost as fat vs ~70% on tirzepatide alone) and was filed under priority review in Aug 2028, with a decision expected 2029.
least_plausible_claims.why: The 2026 world lists bimagrumab only as an adjunct 'in trials', so a full obesity phase 3 that starts, reads out and gets filed with priority review in under two years is very aggressive. The candidate shows no mechanism for that speed, and priority review for a weight-loss combination is a stretch.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Survey self-report puts it at roughly 1 in 5 long-term users describing muted enjoyment at some point, but there is still no prospective trial measuring it.
least_plausible_claims.why: The baseline called reward blunting unquantified and 'uncommon' per clinicians, and the safety_signal driver is 'none'. A precise 20% survey figure appears with no named source or chain, which is an asserted magnitude.

rationale.badness: Access splits into two tiers: coded patients and the cash-comfortable get brand drugs, while uncoded working-class users stay on $149 starter doses or buy imports. About 2.1M people use unapproved product, and the 2027 counterfeit cluster killed four. Cycling and drug holidays are normalised with no controlled data, the 'Ozempic personality' is a mainstream complaint, and Medicaid prescribes the same reward-dampening mechanism for AUD (alcohol use disorder), which the world flags as unmeasured. It is a harder society with new losers, but prices are lower, public payers cover the obesity-only patients they qualify, and nothing has collapsed, so it sits near the middle of the scale.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable. Adoption is exactly 11 to 9.2, employer coverage falls 60% to 44%, and price steps down to $149–299. AUD arrives as a guideline plus a phase 3, the counterfeit and import flood is dated, and Medicaid and Medicare subsidies are in the events. Retatrutide is filed Mar 2027 and approved 14 months later, and the muscle combo is honoured by a priority-review filing, with generic_us staying false. Nothing contradicts a driver. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as coverage loss to cash price to imports to counterfeits, and holidays to point prevalence. Weaker links are the pharma revenue claim, the bimagrumab phase 3 speed, and the 1-in-5 blunting figure (claims 1–3). magnitude: On-drug 9.2 and ever-used 16.0 are inside the envelope, income thirds bracket the national figure, and the age bands weight back to 9.2. The cycling arithmetic reconciles, with 4.8+4.4=9.2 and 31% cycled. The payer mix sums to 24.1M, and both public cost lines multiply out ($4.0B plus $3.8B). The only blemish is the net-price/volume/revenue claim in the pharma economy field.
rationale.generativity: The Marisol vignette shows the world rather than explaining it: the 'coupon dose', skipping the Saturday pill, Beto's Nogales insulin pens, the Medicaid patient at the front desk, and her mother on the Medicare line. The sixteen-year-old son and the open fridge add feeling. The world fields add texture, including the on/off/cycling dating field, Thanksgiving planned around who is 'off that week', 'two-size closet' resale, and Nogales pharmacy errands. A few details are slightly off, such as the Foundayo 'before coffee' instruction.

least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 0.3% of all under-18s is roughly 220k children. The 2026 baseline is about 0.6% of children with obesity, which is on the order of 0.1% of all children. The candidate implies a multi-fold jump in two years, while its prose says children are only 'a little more likely to be prescribed'.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines endorse semaglutide as a second-line pharmacotherapy for alcohol use disorder in adults with obesity; Novo begins AUD phase 3
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a major addiction-medicine guideline plus VA/DoD endorsement arrives about 13 months after a single n=108 Lancet RCT and a phase 2 oral trial, with no unapproved-indication evidence base shown. That is a very fast jump to guideline status, and no chain is given.

least_plausible_claims.quote: planned 'drug holidays' and weekend skipping to restore enjoyment or save money
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: weekly injectables (semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide) have week-long half-lives, so skipping a weekend would not plausibly restore reward by Monday. The world also says appetite returns only in 7–10 days after stopping, which contradicts weekend-scale relief.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe. A two-tier system is visible: coded patients and the cash-comfortable on brand drugs, working-class users stuck at $149 starter doses or on imports ('Nogales pharmacy trips', 2.1M on unapproved product, 4 counterfeit deaths). About 17.8M former users are cycling, with no data on what cycling does, and reward blunting is now a mainstream complaint. Inequality scores highest because bottom-third prevalence is 7.0 vs 11.0 at the top. Flourishing and cohesion are only mildly worse, since holidays and normalisation soften the picture.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable. Adoption is 9.2 (−1.8), employer coverage falls 60→44, AUD arrives via guideline, and counterfeit and generic imports are tied to the Sep 2027 CDC event. The Medicaid subsidy and mainstream_complaint are present, and the muscle combo is realised as a filing under priority review per the approval rules. mechanism: Most chains are shown (employer retreat → 50–64 decline → cash tier → imports). Weaker links are the guideline speed after one small RCT, the pharmacologically odd weekend-skipping story for weekly drugs, and retatrutide launching at $299 cash. These are the claims listed above. magnitude: Everything reconciles. 24.1M users equals 262M × 9.2%, payer mix sums to 24.1M, 1.7M × $195 × 12 ≈ $4.0B and 1.3M × $245 × 12 ≈ $3.8B, the cycled share and income and age weights all check out, and the approval timing respects the 12-month rule. The one soft spot is the pediatric 0.3% jump, which is not envelope-governed.
rationale.generativity: The prose vignette carries real texture: Marisol's 'coupon dose', skipping the Saturday pill, the Nogales pens, the Costco tray bought 'because Saturday', and the sixteen-year-old asking if he'll have to take it. The world fields add implied scenes, including on/off/cycling dating fields, Thanksgiving planned around who is 'off that week', and 'between doses' comedians. It leans slightly on explaining in places, but the film density is high.

least_plausible_claims.quote: US net prices are down about 40% since 2025, volume is flat, and ex-US revenue is lost to generics. Revenue is still growing on new launches, but more slowly than 2026 forecasts.
least_plausible_claims.why: Net prices down 40% with flat volume implies US revenue falls sharply, and current users falling from 11% to 9.2% contradicts 'volume is flat'. Retatrutide's slow, tightly prior-authorised launch and CagriSema's small share cannot fill the gap, so the revenue claim is asserted, not shown (mechanism and magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.quote: because US current-user share fell slightly while ever-user households keep their habits.
least_plausible_claims.why: The stated cause of flattening snack losses is incoherent. It sits against the same world's claim that smaller portions and high-protein formats are 'standard' and 'the norm', and no mechanism links ever-user households to retained demand (mechanism).

least_plausible_claims.quote: The decline is concentrated in 50–64-year-olds with commercial insurance (22%→16%) after employers dropped coverage.
least_plausible_claims.why: A 27% relative fall in one age band is attributed wholesale to a coverage drop, although $149 cash starter doses, brand cash and the gray market are said to absorb uncovered users. The employer-retreat-to-use chain is asserted, not shown, and the figure was backed into the age-weighted arithmetic (mechanism).

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder version of 2026 with new losers. Uncoded working-class users are stuck on non-escalating $149 'coupon doses' or on imports (about 2.1M on unapproved product, a 2027 CDC cluster with 4 deaths). There is also a large cycling population with no controlled data, and a reward-blunting complaint reported by ~1 in 5 long-term users. Medicaid prescribing the same mechanism for AUD adds a mild autonomy concern, but the harms are bounded and discussable, so overall is mid-scale.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible. Adoption is 11→9.2, employer coverage 60→44%, and AUD guidelines, the counterfeit cluster, the Medicaid and Medicare subsidy, the personality layer and normalisation all appear in events. The muscle-preserving combo is realised as a priority-review filing, as the approval rules allow, and safety_signal 'none' is respected by framing the harms as product harms. mechanism: Most chains are shown, but the pharma revenue claim (price −40%, volume flat, revenue growing) and the F&B 'ever-user households keep their habits' explanation are asserted or incoherent, and the 50–64 drop is loosely attributed (claims 1–3). magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope: on-drug 9.2, ever-used 16.0, income thirds averaging 9.2, and the age-weighted sum 9.2. The cycling arithmetic closes, the payer mix sums to 24.1M, and the $4.0B + $3.8B ≈ $7.8B budget math checks. Approval timing is legal (retatrutide 14 months after filing, CagriSema from the Dec 2025 NDA). The only gaps are 'volume is flat' against a falling user share and the pharma revenue statement.
rationale.generativity: The prose vignette is concrete and well populated: Marisol's 'coupon dose', skipping the Saturday pill, the Medicaid patient who sleeps, Beto's Nogales insulin pens, and the son's question. The world fields add scenes of their own, such as Nogales pharmacy errands, Thanksgiving planned around who is 'off that week', 'on / off / cycling' dating profiles, and bars with sober trivia regulars. Daily-life texture is strong and mostly shown rather than explained.

least_plausible_claims.quote: US net prices are down about 40% since 2025, volume is flat, and ex-US revenue is lost to generics.
least_plausible_claims.why: Net price down 40% with flat volume cannot produce growing revenue, and the candidate's own user count fell from about 28.8M (11%) to 24.1M. The 'still growing on new launches' claim is asserted with no arithmetic, so this fails mechanism and reconciliation.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Lilly's bimagrumab + tirzepatide phase 3 read out in Apr 2028 (roughly 90% of weight lost as fat vs ~70% on tirzepatide alone) and was filed under priority review in Aug 2028, with a decision expected 2029.
least_plausible_claims.why: The 2026 world lists bimagrumab only as an adjunct 'in trials', so a full obesity phase 3 that starts, reads out and gets filed with priority review in under two years is very aggressive. The candidate shows no mechanism for that speed, and priority review for a weight-loss combination is a stretch.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Survey self-report puts it at roughly 1 in 5 long-term users describing muted enjoyment at some point, but there is still no prospective trial measuring it.
least_plausible_claims.why: The baseline called reward blunting unquantified and 'uncommon' per clinicians, and the safety_signal driver is 'none'. A precise 20% survey figure appears with no named source or chain, which is an asserted magnitude.

rationale.badness: Access splits into two tiers: coded patients and the cash-comfortable get brand drugs, while uncoded working-class users stay on $149 starter doses or buy imports. About 2.1M people use unapproved product, and the 2027 counterfeit cluster killed four. Cycling and drug holidays are normalised with no controlled data, the 'Ozempic personality' is a mainstream complaint, and Medicaid prescribes the same reward-dampening mechanism for AUD (alcohol use disorder), which the world flags as unmeasured. It is a harder society with new losers, but prices are lower, public payers cover the obesity-only patients they qualify, and nothing has collapsed, so it sits near the middle of the scale.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable. Adoption is exactly 11 to 9.2, employer coverage falls 60% to 44%, and price steps down to $149–299. AUD arrives as a guideline plus a phase 3, the counterfeit and import flood is dated, and Medicaid and Medicare subsidies are in the events. Retatrutide is filed Mar 2027 and approved 14 months later, and the muscle combo is honoured by a priority-review filing, with generic_us staying false. Nothing contradicts a driver. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as coverage loss to cash price to imports to counterfeits, and holidays to point prevalence. Weaker links are the pharma revenue claim, the bimagrumab phase 3 speed, and the 1-in-5 blunting figure (claims 1–3). magnitude: On-drug 9.2 and ever-used 16.0 are inside the envelope, income thirds bracket the national figure, and the age bands weight back to 9.2. The cycling arithmetic reconciles, with 4.8+4.4=9.2 and 31% cycled. The payer mix sums to 24.1M, and both public cost lines multiply out ($4.0B plus $3.8B). The only blemish is the net-price/volume/revenue claim in the pharma economy field.
rationale.generativity: The Marisol vignette shows the world rather than explaining it: the 'coupon dose', skipping the Saturday pill, Beto's Nogales insulin pens, the Medicaid patient at the front desk, and her mother on the Medicare line. The sixteen-year-old son and the open fridge add feeling. The world fields add texture, including the on/off/cycling dating field, Thanksgiving planned around who is 'off that week', 'two-size closet' resale, and Nogales pharmacy errands. A few details are slightly off, such as the Foundayo 'before coffee' instruction.
